Subject: Scheduling: Kaito Energy demo — confirm local day labels

Hi Masa / Sally,

Thanks again for your time earlier. We’d love to schedule a 45-minute demo of Redwood inference tailored to your grid forecasting use case. Proposed slots (I've shown local labels for each city):

- Option A: 2027-06-15 09:00 JST / 09:00 SGT / 11:00 AEST (Sydney)
- Option B: 2027-06-15 22:30 JST / 22:30 SGT / 00:30 AEST (next day in Sydney)
- Option C: 2027-06-15 06:30 JST / 06:30 SGT / 08:30 AEST

Note: Option B falls across midnight for Sydney — I flagged it because we saw a mismatch in an earlier invite where Sydney showed the next day while Tokyo/Singapore still showed the 15th. Can you confirm if you prefer a same-business-day slot for Sydney or OK with the late-night option?

I've attached a short agenda (kaito-demo-agenda.pdf). If you prefer, I can send an invite that uses explicit timezone labels (JST/SGT/AEST) to avoid calendar clients flipping the date.

Best,
Tessa

Cc: Sally Chen <sally.chen@singnet.sg>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 00:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scheduling: Kaito Energy demo — confirm local day labels

Hi Masa — good catch and sorry for the confusion. Quick explanation: our calendar tool was set to AEST as the primary display timezone when the invite was created (that's why the event appeared as 00:30 on 16 Jun for Sydney), while the text in my first email listed times by local clocks. Tokyo and Singapore are both UTC+9 and UTC+8 respectively (they remain on the 15th), whereas Sydney is UTC+10 and crosses to 00:30 on the 16th.

If the Sydney team wants to avoid a next-day label, we should pick Option A or C. Option B is definitely an overnight time for Sydney staff.

Proposed fix: I'll resend the invite with explicit timezone tags in the event summary and include the 'Start time (local)' in the description to avoid client conversions. Alternatively we can choose Option A (11:00 AEST / 09:00 JST/SGT) which keeps the same business day for everyone. Which do you prefer?

Thanks,
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Redwood Inference

Thanks for clarifying, Tessa. From the Sydney ops perspective, anything that shows a next-day date tends to get deprioritized (people assume late night). We prefer Option A at 11:00 AEST on the 15th so it's clearly within office hours in Sydney.

Please resend with explicit timezone text in the invite body and add a short note: "Local time shown as: JST/SGT/AEST" — that helps our calendar clients.

Sally
